test_title: PYST 07: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct to Indirect Speech.

He said, "It must be raining outside."

options.text: He said it should be raining outside.
He said it must be raining outside.
He said it might be raining outside.
He said it had to be raining outside.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He said it might be raining outside.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Modal Verb Conversion:**
 
 
• The modal verb "must" is often converted to "might" in indirect speech when expressing possibility.
 
• This maintains the sense of uncertainty about the situation.
 
 
 
• **Tense:**
 
 
• The tense remains consistent as the sentence is in the present and expresses a general statement.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb "said" remains unchanged as it is appropriate for the context.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Quotation marks are removed in indirect speech.
 
• The statement is integrated smoothly into the sentence after the reporting verb.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *He said it might be raining outside.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He said it should be raining outside." 

 
 
• The modal "should" implies obligation, which changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "He said it must be raining outside." 
 
 
• Direct speech is not converted to indirect speech, as "must" remains unchanged.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said it had to be raining outside." 
 
 
• The phrase "had to be" indicates compulsion or necessity, which changes the meaning of the original sentence.
